suggestions.assertion: The executing piece is inline or a haiku-tier agent, not sonnet/opus/fable
suggestions.reason: This run sidesteps the ambiguity cleanly (it dispatches an explicit haiku Agent and explicitly declines to inherit the session model), but the assertion's 'inline' escape hatch is genuinely ambiguous in this fixture, where the executing session always self-identifies as a top-tier model ('Fable'). Read literally, any baseline run that simply never spawns a subagent -- the default behavior of an unguided agent -- would pass via the 'inline' clause regardless of which model does the work, which is precisely what happened in the without_skill run for this same eval. Consider rephrasing to something that can't be satisfied by 'the session's own large model did it directly,' e.g. 'the model tier that actually performs the edits, whether inline or delegated, is no larger than haiku.'

suggestions.assertion: States all seven complexity scores (S, R, A, K, I, P, V) explicitly with values
suggestions.reason: This only checks that seven lettered values are present, not that they are grounded in an actual finding. This run's scores happen to be well-evidenced (backed by a real grep, cited inline), but a fabricated 'S2 R0 A0 K1 I2 P0 V1' with no supporting search would pass identically. Consider requiring the S score specifically to be traceable to a stated occurrence/file count.

eval_feedback.overall: This run passes all six assertions with substantive, non-coincidental evidence (the scores, the file list, and the routing all independently verify against the live fixture repo). The eval's weak point is assertion 2's phrasing, which only avoided passing a session-model-does-the-work outcome in this run because the run happened to choose delegation, not because the assertion text rules that outcome out unambiguously.
